<details>
The `makepkg --printsrcinfo` command only sources the top-level of the PKGBUILD without executing any function bodies such as `package()`, `build()`, etc. In this file, the global scope consists solely of variable assignments using static or parameterized values derived from the package version, architecture, and GitHub URLs. All variables (e.g., `_ghurl`, `_ghurlraw`, `source`, `sha256sums`) are defined in a straightforward, transparent manner without command substitution, dynamic evaluation (`eval`), or execution of external commands that could lead to unintended code execution or data exfiltration.

There are no top-level invocations of `curl`, `wget`, `bash <(curl ...)`, `eval`, or any other dangerous constructs that would execute during sourcing. The use of GitHub as a source and the inclusion of raw.githubusercontent.com URLs are standard for AUR packages and do not introduce risk during the `--printsrcinfo` phase, as no download or verification occurs at this stage. The checksums are present and not skipped, but even if they were, that would not affect the safety of this specific command.

Thus, sourcing this PKGBUILD for metadata extraction poses no immediate security risk.
</details>
<evidence>

<summary>No dangerous top-level code in PKGBUILD</summary>

No scripts or executable logic are present in this `.SRCINFO` file — it is purely declarative metadata used by the AUR build system. As such, there is no active code to exploit or malicious behavior to trigger. The package adheres to common AUR packaging practices for `-bin` packages that repackage official binaries.

The file does not perform any action by itself and relies on nvchecker, a trusted tool, to interpret it.
